scope: Fifty distinct checking-strength questions, not fifty repeated test invocations or fifty newly discovered bugs.
decision: Ship blocking suppression-integrity policy for the explicitly authorized bypasses; retain declared tool and path boundaries. No autofix or consumer rollout.

passes.question: Can a local Ruff ignore re-enable typing.cast?
passes.result: Required cast policy already ignores source waivers.

passes.question: Can a consumer clear Ruff's selected rules to allow cast?
passes.result: Packaged cast policy remains authoritative.

passes.question: Can a per-file Ruff exclusion permit new cast uses?
passes.result: The required pass runs independently of per-file ignores.

passes.question: Does a bare noqa continue hiding unrelated future findings?
passes.result: Mandatory PGH004 runs with --ignore-noqa.

passes.question: Does a bare type: ignore waive every checker diagnostic?
passes.result: Mandatory PGH003 requires a named code.

passes.question: Can Ruff suppression comments suppress the blanket-suppression rules?
passes.result: Independent packaged pass ignores inline and file waivers.

passes.question: Can a named Ruff rule be disabled for the entire file?
passes.result: SARJ523 rejects scoped file disables; SARJ054 keeps banned-api ownership.

passes.question: Can a disable/enable region authorize future unrelated debt?
passes.result: SARJ523 rejects source range disables.

passes.question: Can bare sarj-noqa waive every Python rule on a line?
passes.result: Bare markers are ineffective and SARJ523 reports them.

passes.question: Can an unscoped pyright: ignore hide all errors on a line?
passes.result: SARJ523 requires an explicit reporter list.

passes.question: Can basic/standard file directives weaken the strict preset?
passes.result: SARJ523 rejects the weaker file modes.

passes.question: Can reportReturnType=false/none erase a real type error?
passes.result: Native probes confirm erasure; SARJ523 rejects these directives.

passes.question: Can warning/information retain visible output while making a real error pass?
passes.result: Native information probe exits 0; all supported sub-error source severities are guarded.

passes.question: Can a non-report boolean switch weaken an annotation contract?
passes.result: Native strictParameterNoneValue=false accepts int=None; the exact demonstrated switch is guarded.

passes.question: Would a broad settings ban reject harmless flags or valid scoped syntax?
passes.result: Unrelated features and named reporter lists with trailing commas remain accepted; unsupported spellings fail upstream.

passes.question: Can strings/docstrings or prose be mistaken for effective directives?
passes.result: Only real comment tokens with directive provenance are checked.

passes.question: Can a code-scoped local exception omit its reason?
passes.result: SARJ419 now reports missing explanations as well as generic ones.

passes.question: Can same/n/a/legacy mechanically satisfy an explanation requirement?
passes.result: The bounded generic-reason vocabulary includes these demonstrated non-reasons.

passes.question: Do chained tool directives, separators or issue hashes hide a missing/vague reason or reject a concrete one?
passes.result: Each directive is inspected, while shared trailing boundary explanations and issue references remain valid.

passes.question: Can suppression-integrity rules waive themselves through sarj-noqa?
passes.result: SARJ054/419/448/523 cannot be locally waived.

passes.question: Can legacy file/code baseline counts grandfather future suppression bypasses?
passes.result: Protected findings are neither recorded nor removed by native baselines.

passes.question: Can a saved canonical fingerprint hide required hygiene after source changes?
passes.result: Required findings carry non-baselineable tags even against existing entries.

passes.question: Can excluded_rules turn off the suppression policy?
passes.result: Required-source-policy findings survive rule exclusions.

passes.question: Can an exclusion override waive required hygiene for one maintained source file?
passes.result: Rule-specific path overrides cannot erase the floor.

passes.question: Are explicitly excluded generated/vendor sources still a valid analysis boundary?
passes.result: Whole-path exclusions are retained; the policy does not claim to analyze excluded source.

passes.question: Can a new @generated header or generated-looking filename authorize its own waiver?
passes.result: Critical Python/TypeScript suppression checks no longer skip source-declared generated files.

passes.question: Can one named exception disable other rules or adjacent source lines?
passes.result: Exact-code and line boundaries remain intact; code prefixes do not match.

passes.question: Can eslint configuration comments turn off every suppression-policing rule before a blanket disable?
passes.result: Reproduced clean ordinary lint; a separate noInlineConfig pass now reports the hygiene violation.

passes.question: Can described file/range disables waive future code?
passes.result: Required eslint-comments/no-use permits only line-local disable forms.

passes.question: Can a local disable omit rule names?
passes.result: Mandatory no-unlimited-disable rejects it independently of source config.

passes.question: Can an exact local rule disable omit the boundary reason?
passes.result: Mandatory require-description preserves the explanation requirement.

passes.question: Can a named line-local exception turn off the checks for exceptions?
passes.result: The independent no-restricted-disable rule protects the hygiene owners.

passes.question: Can @ts-ignore hide unrelated diagnostics even with a description?
passes.result: Required ban-ts-comment rejects ts-ignore.

passes.question: Can @ts-nocheck opt an entire file out of checking?
passes.result: Required ban-ts-comment rejects ts-nocheck.

passes.question: Can @ts-expect-error omit a reason while retaining native suppression semantics?
passes.result: A local expect-error needs a description; concrete local exceptions are retained.

passes.question: Can a generic expect-error reason escape through @generated or inline rule configuration?
passes.result: The custom reason check has no generated-source self-waiver and runs in the independent floor.

passes.question: Can a consumer remove the hygiene plugins/rules from its flat config?
passes.result: The required syntax-only pass supplies its own rule configuration.

passes.question: Can eslint-suppressions.json or canonical debt hide the checks that police suppressions?
passes.result: Required pass disables bulk suppressions; tagged findings survive baselines and rule exclusions.

passes.question: Does hardening accidentally run unrelated rules during explicitly partial checks?
passes.result: Selected ESLint retains configured parser/options/live exceptions; full-only policy is dynamically imported.

passes.question: Can unused-suppression relaxation hide actual required findings, or can partial checks falsely prune unselected debt?
passes.result: Unused counts are computed from ordinary selected/full results before adding the independent floor.

passes.question: Does an unparseable selected Python file yield clean native analysis?
passes.result: Reproduced complete/passed/zero findings; the runner now fails analysis while individual rule APIs may abstain.

passes.question: Can padding a file over 500000 bytes silently omit its checks?
passes.result: The resource cap now reports incomplete analysis instead of silently dropping the file.

passes.question: Can a source read failure after selection look like successful empty analysis?
passes.result: Read errors now propagate to the failed analyzer report.

passes.question: Can disabling Ruff/Pyright make a complete source gate pass a real type error?
passes.result: A blanket capability ban was rejected because explicit tool delegation is a supported boundary, including this preset provider's authored CI. Omitted Python analyzers now receive explicit NOT_REQUESTED coverage notices instead of disappearing.

passes.question: Can disabling ESLint make a complete TypeScript source gate pass @ts-nocheck?
passes.result: Existing NOT_REQUESTED ESLint coverage correctly declares this configured tool boundary. Source-level hygiene is enforced whenever ESLint runs; independent own-CI and partial scopes remain explicit.

passes.question: Could guard output conceal missing ordinary ESLint file results?
passes.result: Ordinary coverage validation is retained; guard results merge only into ordinary results and assert their own selected coverage.

passes.question: Can a fatal parser/configuration message become baselineable ordinary lint debt?
passes.result: Fatal messages remain execution failures, including in the independent pass.

passes.question: Does bare SQL sarj-noqa waive all current and future rules on a line?
passes.result: Bare SQL markers no longer suppress findings; named exact local codes retain their behavior.

passes.question: Does bare HCL sarj-noqa waive all current and future rules on a resource?
passes.result: Bare IaC markers no longer suppress findings; native comment provenance and exact code boundaries are retained.

passes.question: Can static string folding or read-only module namespace extraction bypass the existing cast ban?
passes.result: Native repros escaped the floor. Bounded literal addition/static f-strings and proven typing __dict__/vars/__getattribute__ reads now produce unwaivable cast findings; dynamic/shadowed/mutated identities remain excluded.

limitations: A concrete explanation is not proof that a local exception is justified; only missing and bounded generic reasons are mechanically checked.
Explicit whole-path exclusions, tool delegation, native-only APIs and selected/own-CI checks retain their declared scope. A passing scoped check is not evidence that a delegated analyzer ran.
Runtime-created reflection names, escaped/mutated provider identities and general executable configuration are outside finite static proof.
The independent ESLint pass checks source suppression hygiene; it is not a separate complete TypeScript compiler or arbitrary consumer-configuration equivalence checker.
Checkov and ShellCheck retain native named local suppression ownership. This campaign does not introduce a universal prose validator for every upstream tool.
SQL and IaC exact-code local exceptions retain their native description policy; this campaign removes their bare all-rule waivers.

qualification.inspection: Inspected every natural SARJ523 location and every TypeScript finding location, plus deterministic explanation-omission samples across all corpus batches. Two initial Python prose matches were corrected with native-checker probes and negative regressions. Missing explanations are raw syntactic policy counts, not proof of unsafe exceptions. TypeScript findings include existing upstream no-use policy violations, including inline rule configuration in public ESLint source; those are policy conformance findings, not claims of defects in that project.
qualification.privateEvidence: Four private Git corpus identities, revisions, digests, source text and full observations remain in owner-readable local reports. Public output contains aggregate counts only.
qualification.corpusProtocol: Pinned tracked existing Git content, installed mature public Python/JavaScript packages and positive/negative seeds. Fresh linter process per repository and bounded batch; no process holds multiple repositories.

pythonPerformance.scope: The paired native-runner timings cover final directive-recognition source. Integration-only protected-code casing/severity guards and a behavior-preserving cast-phase/loader-comprehension refactor followed; focused regressions and the full gate provide closure. These are native-runner timings, not end-to-end Ruff/BasedPyright fleet latency measurements.

typescriptPerformance.scope: Ordinary authored ESLint config versus the same config plus required suppression floor, in fresh processes.
